Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings: Acute unilateral throbbing headache with visual aura, photophobia, nausea/vomiting; worsened by movement/leaning forward; prior similar self-limited episode; no fever or rash; denies focal neurologic deficits, balance problems, speech issues, or head trauma. Family history of migraine. On combined OCP for 3 months.  
- Impression: Presentation is most consistent with migraine with visual aura.  
- Differential diagnoses (consistent with DDx):  
  - Migraine with visual aura (high likelihood): Supported by classic aura, unilateral throbbing pain, photophobia, nausea/vomiting, and family history; prior similar episode.  
  - Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) (moderate likelihood): Young woman on combined OCP; headache worse leaning forward with vomiting suggests possible raised intracranial pressure. No focal deficits reported.  
  - Subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) (low likelihood): Acute headache with photophobia/vomiting but no thunderclap onset or neurologic deficits; prior similar episode argues against.  
- Working diagnosis: Migraine with visual aura.  
- Management priorities: Acute symptom relief; headache diary; safety-net advice; plan for follow-up and discussion of preventive therapy if headaches recur or persist.

Management Plan

- Treatments and recommendations provided:  
  - Acute analgesia discussed: acetaminophen (paracetamol) or co-codamol (acetaminophen + codeine); anti-inflammatories such as ibuprofen or naproxen (specific doses not documented).  
  - Headache diary to track frequency, triggers, and response to treatment.  
  - Consider preventive (prophylactic) migraine medication if headaches become frequent or persistent (to be discussed at follow-up).  
  - Safety net: Return urgently if headache worsens or does not improve over 2–3 days, if new neurologic symptoms develop (weakness, speech/vision changes), if neck pain worsens, or if symptoms otherwise escalate.  
  - Follow-up: Suggested next week to review symptoms and discuss prophylaxis.  
- DDx context: While migraine is most likely, DDx highlights CVST risk with combined OCP and positional worsening; not addressed with investigations today in the transcript.

- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Follow-up for headache management planned next week; preventive care otherwise not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

- Migraine with visual aura — High likelihood: Classic unilateral throbbing headache preceded by visual aura, with photophobia and nausea/vomiting; prior similar episode; family history.  
- Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) — Moderate likelihood: New significant headache in a young woman on a combined OCP; worse with leaning forward and associated vomiting suggest possible raised intracranial pressure; no focal deficits reported.  
- Subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) — Low likelihood: Acute headache with photophobia/vomiting, but no thunderclap onset or neurologic deficits; prior similar episode argues against.

- Missing clinically expected elements: Vitals (BP, pulse); full neurologic exam (cranial nerves, motor/sensory, reflexes, gait); fundoscopic exam for papilledema; vision testing (acuity/fields); pregnancy status; BMI/weight; urinalysis; medication allergies; immunization review; detailed medication dosing/instructions; mental health screening (PHQ-2/9, anxiety screening); alcohol/substance use details beyond yes/no; preventive screening status (cervical screening, STI screen).  
- Internal contradictions: Transcript reassures against serious causes; DDx raises moderate concern for CVST due to OCP and positional features—potential risk not addressed with investigations in the transcript.  
- Transcript quality: Some lines were incomplete/unclear; examination and vital signs not documented.
